description: Share of the material entering this step that leaves it as usable output (the rest is waste)
source: PROTOTYPE machine assumed: ~1 m3 electric convection oven (1 m x 2 m x 0.5 m chamber), modelled on the Memmert UF1060 (1,060 L, 7 kW connected load, 252 kg, up to 300 C; memmert.com UF1060 page and datasheet). Yield = dry mass share of the wet printed paste. Evidence: printable earth/clay mixes hold 20-37 wt% water, i.e. 63-80% yield (MDPI Buildings 2026, 16(6), 1261; review of clay/sawdust printing, water/dry ratio 0.37-0.58 = 27-37 wt% water, ScienceDirect S2590123024012799); a printable wood-cellulose-lignin ink lost 74% of its mass on drying, i.e. 26% yield (PMC10942110). Fibrous, protein-bound pastes (sawdust, seagrass, pea protein) need more water than earth, so the low-to-middle of that range is used.
comments: Was 70%. 70% is the top of the earth-mixture range; a lignocellulosic paste is closer to 40-60%. NEEDS THE ACTUAL RECIPE: please replace with (dry mass / wet paste mass) from the lab. Water is included in the mass basis of all upstream steps (wet basis). Residual moisture in the dried product (~5-10%) is not modelled. Two sources on bio-based pastes (WUR report, Springer wood LDM paper) could not be read (rate limit).

description: Share of the product's end-of-life mass that goes to this route (the routes add up to 100 %): composted
source: Eurostat 2018 non-hazardous biogenic waste EU28: 79% recycled (composting, biogas), 16.1% energy recovery, 2.8% incinerated, 1.5% landfilled (Treatment and valorization of bio-waste in the EU, ScienceDirect); EU 2022: separately captured bio-waste 46%, food waste 26% (Zero Waste Europe / BIC); EU municipal waste 2023 recycling 47.7% (EEA); ECN: municipal solid waste treated 17% composting/AD, 27% incineration, 24% landfill. Targets: separate collection of bio-waste mandatory in the EU from 2024; municipal recycling 55% by 2025 (EEA), 65% and max 10% landfill by 2035 (Waste Framework/Landfill Directives, from general knowledge, not re-checked online).
comments: Typical: municipal bio-waste captured separately ~46% (2022) minus rejects = ~42% composted or digested (anaerobic digestion is counted here, no separate route). Max 79% = Eurostat all-sector biogenic waste. Scaled-up: mandatory separate collection and the 65% recycling target push this to ~55%. NOTE: methods.md says the scaled-up variant leaves end of life unchanged, so these scaled_up values are stored here but may not be read by the model.
